What exactly IS a digital product? Let me break down every type — with examples. If you've been seeing people talk about 'selling digital products' and wondering what they're actually selling — this is for you. A digital product is anything you create once and sell repeatedly — delivered instantly online, no shipping, no inventory, no returns. Here are the main types: 📄 EBOOKS & GUIDES — PDFs that teach something specific. 'Beginner's Guide to Instagram,' '30-Day Content Plan,' 'How to Start Affiliate Marketing.' Sell for $7–$47. Create in Canva for free. 🎨 TEMPLATES — Pre-made designs buyers customize. Instagram templates, planners, resumes, business cards. Sell for $9–$97. Create in Canva. 🎓 COURSES & WORKSHOPS — Video or written lessons teaching a skill. Can sell for $47–$997+. Host on Stan Store or Beacons. 📦 DONE-FOR-YOU PRODUCTS (PLR/MRR) — Products already created that you can resell. Perfect for beginners who aren't ready to create from scratch yet. 📋 PLANNERS, WORKBOOKS & PRINTABLES — Fillable or printable pages. Budget planners, habit trackers, goal workbooks. Sell for $5–$37. These get the most saves and shares on social. The best part? You don't have to create anything to start. You can begin with a done-for-you product while you're still learning — then create your own once you understand what your audience actually wants. Save this. Want to create and sell digital products? Here's what you actually do. 👇  1. Start with a problem. What problem are you solving for someone else? The best digital products make something easier, faster, or less overwhelming. 2. Create the solution. Turn what you know into something useful—a guide, checklist, planner, workbook, template, printable, mini-course, or resource. 3. Choose where to sell it. You can sell digital products through platforms like Etsy, Teachers Pay Teachers, Stan Store, or your own website. Choose the platform that makes sense for your product and audience. You can also publish them on Amazon Kindle Direct Publishing or Google Play.  4. Market it. Creating the product is only HALF the job. People have to find it! Use Pinterest, TikTok,  email, a blog, or search-friendly content to show people how your product solves their problem. 5. Learn from the first one...then create another. Your first product doesn't have to build financial freedom. It's your starting point. Create one useful product. Learn how to sell it. Improve. Then create another. Over time, you can build a collection of digital products that can be purchased while you're teaching, spending time with family, or simply living your life.
